pairs.reason: A keeps the horror inside one domestic detail and a professional's refusal to name it, while B's stronger central image arrives through an object the story never installs.
pairs.strength_A: Emotional credibility is produced by evidence rather than stated: "She never washed up" converts a cup into a verdict, and Ray's flat "Mind how you go" withholds the report.
pairs.defect_A: A few slack triplets do no work, the worst being "cold and dry and old" at the door, where one precise noun would have carried more.
pairs.strength_B: The physical detail is exact and diagnostic: "her breath go in and stay there" does the work the paragraph never explains.
pairs.defect_B: The closing image depends on an unestablished object: "the bolt, the new bolt, going home" is a cause supplied after the effect, since he drilled the housing out and only ever fitted a cylinder.
pairs.notes: B runs 1101 words against 'around 900' and ends in a second location (the van outside), hence brief_ok false; craft scores unaffected.

pairs.reason: A's convergence runs through one repeated act, signing without looking, where B's runs through coincidence and echoed similes, which makes A the more disciplined chapter even though it badly under-serves its courtroom line.
pairs.strength_A: The three lines are knotted by a single verb: "взяла ручку и подписала, не читая" pays off in the verdict's opening formula, and no explanation is offered.
pairs.defect_A: The trial, which is a third of the brief and the emotional engine, is reduced to summary: "На процессе Кирилл поднял руку" is the whole of it, so the finale carries weight the chapter has not prepared.
pairs.strength_B: Nina's self-deception is enacted, not stated: "сдвинула их обратно, на котлету" hides the uneaten food the same way she hides the case.
pairs.defect_B: The convergence is engineered through repetition, not event: the "маленький твёрдый квадрат, туго сложенный вчетверо" appears three times, and the portrait from Olga's flat turning up in Grigory's studio is a coincidence the chapter never causes.
pairs.notes: A is 910 words against 1400-1800 and B is 1387; A's shortfall is recorded here, not in the craft scores.

pairs.reason: A stays inside the brief's discipline and lets a flat-pack wardrobe and a fence carry eleven years of marriage, while B reaches the same ache but keeps stepping out of dialogue to explain the marriage to the reader.
pairs.strength_A: The unsaid thing is said as an object: "Put it in the sink when you get in" is a kindness neither of them will name, and the four-pack on the seat finishes it.
pairs.defect_A: One clause of narration does history the scene should have implied: "the lager she used to have on a Friday" reaches past the smallest possible action.
pairs.strength_B: The wristband is handled with total restraint: "Tape goes funny. Leaves a mark." is the closest either of them comes, and it is enough.
pairs.defect_B: The narration keeps breaking the dialogue-only frame to supply backstory: "eaten every morning for eleven years" tells the reader what the scene had already shown.
pairs.notes: Neither text uses love/hate/sorry/miss; B is under 600 words but its narration exceeds 'the smallest possible amount of action', so brief_ok is false.

pairs.reason: A makes the clock a live argument between two people and closes on a genuine reversal, while B's finer single invention sits in a chapter whose arithmetic and final image are both less secure.
pairs.strength_A: Brandt's self-defence is the best exchange in the set: "That's not loyalty. That's bookkeeping." answers her accusation and reveals him in five words.
pairs.defect_A: The last line steps outside the scene to announce its own theme: "Eleven minutes and a woman's whole life" is the chapter summarising itself.
pairs.strength_B: The ledger's private column is a real discovery, concrete and legible: "Every pencil figure sat eleven minutes before" the times copied off the wall.
pairs.defect_B: One word does two jobs badly, since "You'd come off the bar at three" reads as a pub while "the bar" two lines later is the sandbar.
pairs.notes: Both keep the bible's facts and add no named characters; A is 1593 words against a 1600 ceiling.

pairs.reason: B rewrites the ending into something concrete and controls every sentence, while A leaves the draft's flattest sentence standing and then claims in its note to have fixed it.
pairs.strength_A: One clause turns stated grief into behaviour: "she had stopped noticing, except when she breathed" is the best sentence in either revision.
pairs.defect_A: The original's abstract close survives almost intact: "not as a thought but as a fact" is still the narration telling the reader what she knows.
pairs.strength_B: The replacement ending is concrete and belongs to this street: "She had stood here before, in other weather." earns the decision that follows it.
pairs.defect_B: The brief asks for the same events, and the new decision substitutes a different knowledge for the original's: "would not come back down it" is a change of event, however well written.
pairs.notes: Both explanations are under 120 words (94 and 113). A's note describes a fix the text did not make, which affected the preference.

pairs.reason: A dramatizes the humiliation and then refuses both the compliment and the catharsis, while B's sharper texture is carried by a reported humiliation and a town inventory.
pairs.strength_A: The teacher's kindness is made the cruellest fact: "Зла она ему не желала" costs him more than malice would, and the last line refuses to resolve it.
pairs.defect_A: The funeral is peopled with types rather than persons, e.g. "мужики с лопатами стояли в стороне", so the present-day frame is thinner than the flashback it holds.
pairs.strength_B: Post-Soviet decay is rendered as fact without nostalgia: "все лица сбиты, остались белые пятна" on the square's panno, and the smell of the school that does not move him.
pairs.defect_B: One beat slips into the nostalgia the brief forbids: "Котлета была сухая, как в детстве" makes the canteen food a childhood echo rather than a present fact.
pairs.notes: Both are within 1000-1300 and neither offers catharsis or forgiveness.

notes: Axis mapping used, per the task's six axes rather than the rubric's twelve: narrative_coherence covers rubric 1 plus causal consistency (4) and continuity (12) where they bear on the story's spine; character merges depth (2) and agency (3); prose covers 7 with dialogue (6) and style consistency (11) folded in; emotional_credibility is 8; originality is 9; structural_integrity is 10 with temporal handling (5) folded in where relevant. Scores were assigned text-by-text before any preference. Word counts exclude the revision notes in pair-7 and count only letter/number tokens (Russian em-dashes inflate whitespace counts by roughly 8-9% in the Russian texts). Two things the analyst should know. First, five of six preferences went to A, and A-texts in this set are systematically sparser; I re-tested each pair specifically for a plainness bias against dense prose and kept the preference only where the denser text had a defect on the page (pair-1: an object never installed; pair-2: coincidental convergence; pair-4: narration outside the dialogue-only frame; pair-6: a word collision and an unresolved closing image; pair-9: a reported humiliation). Pair-7 is the one where the denser text won, on the strength of its rewritten ending. Second, brief compliance is recorded but unscored, and it cuts both ways: pair-2's A is 910 words against 1400-1800 and pair-1's B is 1101 against 'around 900', so neither preferred text in those pairs is the compliant one on length. Scores on pair-1's B and pair-9's B sit in a narrow band; that is a reading of uniformly competent texts with no axis of excellence, not an averaging of auras.
